long_biography.plain_text:
An electronics engineer from Genoa, Bisagno entered T. Mariotti in 1973 after marrying into the founder's family. He progressed from technical director to chief executive and helped the yard move beyond repair work into passenger-ship conversions and luxury newbuildings. In 1992, he and Paolo Zanetti acquired equal shares in the company. That transfer gave Bisagno ownership of an established family enterprise, while his subsequent operating record materially broadened its scale and specialisation.

Combining T. Mariotti with San Giorgio del Porto under Genova Industrie Navali created a larger shipbuilding and repair group. He remains chairman of both the holding company and T. Mariotti, although day-to-day management has passed to other executives. Shipbuilding is therefore both the sector that produced his wealth and his current principal business. His relationship is best described as operator because he did not establish the original yard, yet spent decades directing and expanding it. Historical reports describe Bisagno and Zanetti jointly controlling the Mariotti side of the holding; they do not disclose his current individual percentage. Group turnover, facilities, contracts, orderbooks and subsidiary assets belong to the companies rather than to him personally.

Marriage / family transfer captures access to the core asset; his decades of subsequent expansion are recorded separately as operator achievement.

Temistocle Mariotti founded the original yard long before Bisagno entered it. Bisagno later helped form Genova Industrie Navali, but the transferred T. Mariotti stake remains the core wealth-producing asset, so Operator is more precise than Founder.

Bisagno remains chairman of Genova Industrie Navali and T. Mariotti, while current sources identify different executives as chief executives. Chairmanship demonstrates continuing strategic involvement but should not be confused with sole day-to-day management.
